issues: Narration omits the reported preparation and expectation in verse 2; the summary correctly notes those events are recounted, not shown. The unspecified narration setting could still imply an unsupported setting if visualized.
The verses do not identify the speaker as Nephi; labeling the speaker Nephi is uncertain. The source gives the speech but does not establish that the addressed inhabitants are physically present.

The note identifying Nephi as the chapter’s first-person narrator is unsupported by the supplied verses. The preceding scene also identifies Nephi as the speaker without support; the current scene correctly leaves the speaker unidentified.
The claim that the Lord of Hosts says the houses will be desolate is an interpretation of “In mine ears, said the Lord of Hosts”; the verse does not explicitly identify him as the speaker.
The inference that unnamed people are shown at a feast is plausible but not certain: the warning describes their feasts, without establishing a particular visible occasion.
The summary says the addressed people “take away the righteousness”; the verse states that they take it away from the righteous, which should be preserved if paraphrasing.
The scene reports physical smiting and torn carcasses. Any depiction must remain non-graphic and must not stage the reported event as happening anew.
